mainTopic: Whether we worry that a woman saw blood during בין השמשות, how רבי decides between רבי יהודה בן אגרא and the חכמים, and how two ברייתות about this are reconciled.
overview: A woman's sighting of blood might have happened during בין השמשות, which could count as seeing on two days. רבי יהודה בן אגרא, quoting רבי יוסי, worries about this, and the חכמים do not. רבי says each side is right in a different case: when she did not check, and when she did. רבא reports how the רבנן of רב's study hall explained this: she checked all through רבי יהודה's longer twilight but not during רבי יוסי's final moment, which the רבנן treat as night and רבי יוסי treats as a doubt. The גמרא then reads רבי's words on its own and finds that his two halves seem to contradict each other. It resolves this by explaining that רבי is describing where the חכמים actually argue: everyone worries if she never checked, and they argue only about checking during רבי יהודה's twilight alone. A second ברייתא about a כתם, where רבי gives a stricter version of רבי יוסי's view, makes רבי יהודה בן אגרא lenient in that same in-between case, so he seems to contradict himself. The גמרא answers that two תנאים report his view differently, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי splits the case between the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי rules that רבי יהודה בן אגרא is right when the woman did not check, and the חכמים are right when she did check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה בן אגרא's view makes sense when she did not check, and the חכמים' view makes sense when she did check.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי settles the argument by saying that each side is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן אגרא worries that she saw blood at twilight. The חכמים do not worry. רבי says the worry is reasonable only if she did not check, but he does not yet explain what kind of checking he means.

keyTerms.meaning: the words seem correct, a phrase for deciding between opinions
she checked (did a בְּדִיקָה for blood)
the Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra seem correct
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא. רבי יהודה בן אגרא is the one who worries she saw at twilight.

phrases.english: where she did not examine,
and the words of the Sages, where she did examine.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worry about seeing at twilight applies when she did not check, and it does not apply when she did check.

steps.title: What counts as checking and not checking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי means by 'she checked' and 'she did not check'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'she checked' and what is 'she did not check'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear definition of רבי's two cases. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she simply checked and found nothing, it seems obvious there is nothing to worry about. So the גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of partial checking רבי has in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: what? (a request to explain)

phrases.english: What is 'she examined,' and what is 'she did not examine'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the terms in רבי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situations of 'checked' and 'did not check' in רבי's ruling.

steps.title: She checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not רבי יוסי's
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that the רבנן of רב's study hall explained the case: she checked her body but not her garment, and only during רבי יהודה's twilight, not during רבי יוסי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I found the Sages of רב's study hall sitting and saying: The case is where she checked herself but not her garment. Even herself, she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight, and not during רבי יוסי's twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reporting an explanation he heard from the scholars in רב's study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different definitions of בין השמשות. רבי יהודה's is a longer period that starts earlier. רבי יוסי's is only a blink of an eye, right before night. She checked during the first period and not during the second, so the case is 'checked' by one definition and 'not checked' by the other.

keyTerms.meaning: with what are we dealing here? (introduces a specific case)
twilight, a time of doubt between day and night
her garment/robe
the scholars of רב's study hall

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'twilights' here. רבי יהודה's is earlier and longer. רבי יוסי's is a split second at the very end, right before night. She checked during the first and not during the second.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
phrases.english: Rava said: I found the Sages of the house of Rav
sitting and saying:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where she examined herself,
but did not examine her robe,
and even herself she did not examine
except during the twilight of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא בָּדְקָה.
phrases.english: but during the twilight of Rabbi Yosei she did not examine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She checked her body only during רבי יהודה's twilight, not her garment and not during רבי יוסי's twilight.

steps.title: Why each side rules the way it does
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that רבי יוסי's twilight is already night, so her check was enough. רבי יוסי holds that his twilight is a doubt, so the unchecked moment is a worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that רבי יוסי's twilight is night, and she did check during רבי יהודה's twilight. רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning, since he says that twilight is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars finish their explanation by showing why each opinion fits this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the moment she did not check already counts as night, so the time she checked covered all of twilight. For רבי יוסי, whose ruling רבי יהודה בן אגרא reports, that final moment is an uncertain time. Since she did not check then, we worry she saw blood then.

keyTerms.meaning: it is night
following his own reasoning
a doubt, an uncertain status

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on how each side defines the final moment of twilight: night (the רבנן) or a doubt (רבי יוסי).

phrases.english: For the Rabbis hold

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֵילְיָא הוּא,
phrases.english: that during the twilight of Rabbi Yosei it is night,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בָּדְקָה בְּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and she did examine during the twilight of Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Yosei follows his reasoning,
for he said twilight is a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the case defined in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on whether רבי יוסי's twilight counts as night or as a doubt.

steps.title: רבא: maybe she saw the moment she stopped checking
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the scholars: unless she checked for the entire twilight, she might have seen blood right when she stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to them: If her hands had been there for the whole twilight, you would be right. But now, maybe she saw just as she removed her hands?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the explanation of the רבנן of רב's study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A check only proves there was no blood while she was checking. If she stopped during רבי יהודה's twilight, there is still time left before night when blood could come. So even by the רבנן's view, a worry seems to remain.

keyTerms.meaning: if only, had it been
her hands in her 'eyes,' a polite way of saying she was checking her body
the removal of her hands

phrases.english: And I said to them:
Had her hands been in her eyes
phrases.notes: 'Her eyes' is a polite way of referring to her private area, where she checks.

phrases.english: the entire twilight,
you would be speaking well,

phrases.aramaic: עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁמָּא עִם סִלּוּק יָדֶיהָ רָאֲתָה?
phrases.english: but now, perhaps with the removal of her hands she saw?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ אֲנָא: אִילְמָלֵי יָדֶיהָ בְּעֵינֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case defined in steps 3-4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that checking during רבי יהודה's twilight removes all worry for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A check covers only the time she was checking. Once she stopped, blood could still have come before night.

steps.title: She checked for the whole twilight
steps.stepSummary: The scholars answer that the case is where she kept checking for the entire twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to me: When we said this, it was about a case where she kept her hands there for the whole twilight.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars answer רבא's challenge by making the case more precise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She checked for all of רבי יהודה's twilight, so for the רבנן no time was left unchecked. The only gap is רבי יוסי's final moment, which the רבנן treat as night and רבי יוסי treats as a doubt. That keeps the argument exactly where they placed it.

keyTerms.meaning: when we said it, we meant
she placed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling refers to a woman who checked throughout רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's final moment. The רבנן are not worried, and רבי יוסי (through רבי יהודה בן אגרא) is worried.

phrases.english: And they said to me:
When we said it,
it was where she placed her hands in her eyes
the entire twilight.
phrases.notes: He means the whole twilight of רבי יהודה, as in step 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She checked only briefly during רבי יהודה's twilight, so a gap remained.
steps.terutzMaskana: She checked for the whole of רבי יהודה's twilight. Only רבי יוסי's final moment went unchecked.

steps.title: The גמרא Re-Examines רבי's Words: What Does 'She Did Not Check' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי again: רבי יהודה בן אגרא's view seems right when she did not check. It then asks what exactly 'she did not check' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: The view of רבי יהודה בן אגרא seems correct in a case where she did not check. What does 'she did not check' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי's statement and asks for the exact meaning of 'she did not check.' This sets up the next steps, where it will try out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees with the strict view of רבי יהודה בן אגרא, which says she must worry she saw blood at twilight, but only when she did not check. There are two twilight periods in play, the one of רבי יהודה and the one of רבי יוסי. So 'did not check' is unclear: did she skip one of them or both?

keyTerms.meaning: 'The words of ... seem correct,' a way of agreeing with one view
She checked herself for blood
Twilight, the in-between time when it is unclear whether it is still day or already night

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of steps 2-3. There, the רבנן of רב's study hall gave their own explanation. Here the גמרא starts its own fresh reading of רבי's words.

phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words appear [correct]

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא כְּשֶׁלֹּא בָּדְקָה.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra, where she did not check.
What is meant by "she did not check"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי's statement to analyze it directly, separate from the explanation of the רבנן of רב's study hall
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which twilight period(s) she failed to check in, in רבי's case of 'she did not check'

steps.title: First Reading Rejected: She Checked Only During רבי יהודה's Twilight
steps.stepSummary: Suppose 'did not check' means she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's. Then רבי יהודה בן אגרא would make her worry even when she checked through both periods. That makes no sense, because she checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's, that would imply that רבי יהודה בן אגרא holds she must worry even though she checked in both. But she checked!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out one reading of 'she did not check' and shows that it leads to an impossible result, so it drops it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי agrees with רבי יהודה בן אגרא only when she missed רבי יוסי's twilight, then רבי יהודה בן אגרא's own ruling must go further than that. It would have to cover even a woman who checked during both twilights. But a woman who checked the whole time and found nothing has no reason to worry, so this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say...', which introduces a suggested reading that will be tested
'By implication', what follows from what was just said
She must worry (be concerned that she saw blood)
In both of them (both twilight periods)

phrases.english: If you say that she checked during [the twilight] of Rabbi Yehuda,
but did not check during [the twilight] of Rabbi Yosei,
then by implication Rabbi Yehuda holds:
phrases.notes: This 'רבי יהודה' is רבי יהודה בן אגרא, the one with the strict view, not the רבי יהודה whose twilight was just mentioned.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּבָדְקָה בְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ חָיְישָׁא?
phrases.english: even though she checked during both, she must worry?
But she checked!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 7 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'did not check' means she skipped only רבי יוסי's twilight
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would force רבי יהודה בן אגרא to make her worry even after she checked through both twilights, which is unreasonable

steps.title: The Correct Reading: She Checked During Neither Twilight
steps.stepSummary: 'Did not check' must mean she checked during neither twilight. If she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's, she does not need to worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means she did not check at all, neither during רבי יהודה's twilight nor during רבי יוסי's. But if she checked during רבי יהודה's and not during רבי יוסי's, she does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reading that works: רבי sides with the strict view only when she skipped checking entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first reading falls, the only option left is that she checked during neither period. This also tells us something new about the in-between case. If she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight, רבי holds she has nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, it is obvious...', which brings the reading that replaces a rejected one
She does not need to worry

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that she did not check,

phrases.aramaic: לָא בִּדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא בִּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: neither during Rabbi Yehuda's [twilight] nor during Rabbi Yosei's;
but if she checked during Rabbi Yehuda's
and did not check during Rabbi Yosei's —
she does not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading rejected in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Did not check' means she checked in neither twilight. Checking only during רבי יהודה's twilight is enough to remove the worry.

steps.title: Inference: For רבי, רבי יוסי's Twilight Is Night
steps.stepSummary: Since checking only during רבי יהודה's twilight is enough, רבי must treat רבי יוסי's twilight as night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently, according to רבי, the twilight of רבי יוסי is night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from step 9 about how רבי views רבי יוסי's twilight. This conclusion will be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing a check during רבי יוסי's twilight does not matter to רבי. The only explanation is that he considers that time to be night already, not a doubtful time. This matches the view of the רבנן in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Evidently', which introduces a conclusion drawn from what came before
Night

steps.whatToRemember: According to the reading in step 9, רבי holds that the בין השמשות of רבי יוסי is already night, so a woman who checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight does not need to worry.

phrases.english: Evidently, the twilight of Rabbi Yosei
according to Rabbi is night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי לֵילְיָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general conclusion from the reading given in step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי treats רבי יוסי's בין השמשות as night

steps.title: Testing the Second Half: What Does 'She Checked' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second half of רבי's statement, 'the words of the חכמים apply where she checked,' and asks what 'she checked' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now say the latter part: 'And the words of the חכמים apply where she checked.' What does 'she checked' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the second half of רבי's statement to see whether it fits the conclusion just reached. This sets up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי treats רבי יוסי's twilight as night, then the case of 'she checked' in the second half should match that view. By asking what 'she checked' means, the גמרא is getting ready to show a tension with the reading it just built.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the latter clause', which brings the next part of a statement to test a reading
The Sages, here the lenient side of the dispute

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
"And the words of the Sages [appear correct] where she checked."
What is meant by "she checked"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the conclusion of step 10 against the second half of רבי's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case 'she checked' refers to in the second half of רבי's statement, given the reading of the first half

steps.title: Checking only during רבי יהודה's twilight cannot be what 'she checked' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests whether 'she checked' means she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not רבי יוסי's. It rejects this because the חכמים would then say 'no worry' even when she checked during neither, and in that case she did not check at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose 'she checked' means she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's. Then we would have to conclude that the חכמים hold there is no worry even when she did not check during both twilights. But in that case she did not check at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning of 'she checked' and shows that it leads to a ridiculous result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 9, 'did not check' means she checked during neither twilight. If 'checked' meant only רבי יהודה's twilight, then רבי sides with the חכמים only in that case, and the case of checking during neither is left inside the argument with the חכמים saying 'no worry.' Saying there is nothing to worry about when she never checked makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא is testing a possible reading)
By implication, from this it follows
We are not worried
In both of them (both twilight periods)

phrases.english: If you say that she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight,
but did not check during רבי יוסי's twilight,
it would follow that the חכמים hold

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא בָּדְקָה בְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ
phrases.english: that even though she did not check during both of them,
we are not worried.
But she did not check!

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא דבדקה בדרבי יהודה ולא בדקה בדרבי יוסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'she checked' means only during רבי יהודה's twilight
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would leave the חכמים saying 'no worry' in a case where she never checked at all

steps.title: 'She checked' means she checked during both twilights
steps.stepSummary: So 'she checked' must mean she checked during both twilights. It follows that if she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight, we do worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that 'she checked' means she checked during both רבי יהודה's twilight and רבי יוסי's twilight. But if she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight and not during רבי יוסי's, we are worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the meaning of 'she checked' that works: she checked during both twilights. It then draws a result from this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי sides with the חכמים only when she checked during both periods, the in-between case, where she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight, is left with the worry. This result sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Both... and...
We are worried; we take the possibility seriously

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that she checked
both during רבי יהודה's twilight
and during רבי יוסי's twilight.
But if she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight
and did not check during רבי יוסי's twilight,
we are worried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the meaning that is left after step 12 rejected the first one
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'she checked' means in רבי's statement
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She checked during both twilights, so checking during only רבי יהודה's twilight still leaves a worry

steps.title: רבי's two statements contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: From step 13, רבי treats רבי יוסי's twilight as a doubt. Step 10 showed that he treats it as night. These two results clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: So for רבי, רבי יוסי's twilight is a doubtful time. Then one statement of רבי contradicts another statement of רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from step 13 and shows that it contradicts what it learned from the first half of רבי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If checking only during רבי יהודה's twilight still leaves a worry, then רבי must think רבי יוסי's twilight might be day, so it is a doubt. But in step 10, the first half of רבי's words showed he treats that same time as night. The same person cannot hold both.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see
Twilight, the in-between time after sunset
A doubt; it might be day or night
There is a contradiction between two statements of רבי

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different twilights here. רבי יהודה's twilight comes first. רבי יוסי's twilight is a very short moment that comes later. The whole question is how רבי treats that later moment.

phrases.english: Evidently, רבי יוסי's twilight
is a doubtful time according to רבי.
Then one statement of רבי contradicts another statement of רבי!
phrases.notes: The first half (step 10) showed he treats רבי יוסי's twilight as night; this half shows he treats it as a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלמא בין השמשות דרבי יוסי לרבי ספקא הוי קשיא דרבי אדרבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 13 and sets it against step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half shows that רבי יוסי's twilight is night for רבי, and the second half shows it is a doubt for him

steps.title: רבי is describing where the חכמים actually argue
steps.stepSummary: רבי means that even the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה בן אגרא when she did not check at all. They argue only when she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight and not during רבי יוסי's. So 'she checked' means checking during רבי יהודה's twilight is enough, and there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי is saying: the חכמים themselves think רבי יהודה בן אגרא is right when she did not check at all, neither during רבי יהודה's twilight nor during רבי יוסי's. Even the חכמים argue with him only when she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight and not during רבי יוסי's. But when she did not check at all, they agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by rereading רבי's words. They describe exactly where the חכמים argue and where they agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is not giving his own split between the two sides. He is reporting the actual argument: when she never checked, everyone worries. The argument is only about checking during רבי יהודה's twilight alone, and there the חכמים say no worry, which fits treating רבי יוסי's twilight as night, as in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a rereading of the statement)
At all
They did not argue
They agree with him

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees there is a worry if she never checked. The חכמים argue with רבי יהודה בן אגרא only when she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not רבי יוסי's. In that case they say no worry, because רבי יוסי's twilight counts as night. This keeps רבי consistent.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: The words of רבי יהודה בן אגרא seem right to the חכמים
when she did not check at all,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא בִּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: not during רבי יהודה's twilight and not during רבי יוסי's.
For even the חכמים did not argue with him
except where she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight
and did not check during רבי יוסי's twilight.
But where she did not check at all,
they agree with him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יהודה בן אגרא, so in that case we do worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי קאמר נראין דברי רבי יהודה בן אגרא לרבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement as a report of where the two sides agree and where they argue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי was splitting between the two sides, so 'she checked' had to mean both twilights
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה בן אגרא when she never checked and argue only when she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight alone, which fits treating רבי יוסי's twilight as night

steps.title: A contradicting ברייתא about a stain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a woman who finds a large כתם worries, and one who finds a small כתם does not. This is רבי יהודה בן אגרא's view, quoting רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A woman who sees a stain: if it is a large stain, she must worry. If it is a small stain, she does not need to worry. This is what רבי יהודה בן אגרא said in the name of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a contradiction by quoting a new ברייתא. This step only sets things up; the clash becomes clear in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The subject switches from actually seeing blood to finding a כתם. רבי יהודה בן אגרא is lenient about a small stain. רבי's different version and the meaning of 'checked' come next. They will show a clash between this ruling of רבי יהודה בן אגרא and his ruling in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they raised a contradiction': a source is brought that seems to clash with what was just said
A stain of blood found on a garment or body, as opposed to blood she felt come out
A large sighting or a small sighting, meaning a big stain or a small stain
She must worry, meaning she has to be concerned about the stricter status

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A woman who sees a stain,
for a large sighting, she worries;
phrases.notes: A 'large sighting' means a big stain, big enough to count as more than one day's worth of seeing.

phrases.english: for a small sighting, she does not worry.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא
phrases.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra
who said it in the name of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15 by bringing a parallel ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה בן אגרא: in the first ברייתא (as explained in steps 3-4 and 15), he worries when she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight, so for him רבי יוסי's twilight is a doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read the same way as before, this ברייתא shows רבי יהודה בן אגרא is lenient when she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight. That treats רבי יוסי's twilight as night, against his strict position in the first ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי's version: she worries in both cases, if she checked
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he heard from רבי יוסי that she worries about both a large and a small stain. The reason: a נדה who did not check herself from מנחה onward is still presumed impure. רבי adds that this view is correct where she checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: I heard from him that in both cases, large stain or small, she worries. He gave me this reason: if a נדה did not do her purity check from מנחה time onward, wouldn't she still be presumed impure? And his words seem right where she checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי's different version of רבי יוסי's view. He is strict in both cases and limits it with 'where she checked.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason is that without a check, we cannot assume she was clean, so the stain counts against her. The closing words 'where she checked' are the same phrase the גמרא already analyzed in the first ברייתא. That is why the same question is about to be asked again.

keyTerms.meaning: She separated in purity, meaning she did the check that shows her bleeding has stopped
The afternoon, the time of the מנחה offering
A presumption of impurity: we keep treating her as impure until shown otherwise

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
I heard from him
that in both this case and that case she worries,
and he told it to me for this reason:
And what if a menstruating woman
did not separate in purity
from מנחה time onward —
would she not be presumed impure?
And his words appear correct where she checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא opened in step 16 with רבי's competing version
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי's report of רבי יוסי, she worries about any stain, large or small, and this is correct where she checked

steps.title: What does 'she checked' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'she checked' means in this ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she checked' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked in step 11, now about this ברייתא. It is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two twilights, רבי יהודה's earlier one and רבי יוסי's later one. The question is which twilight she must have checked during.

keyTerms.meaning: She checked: she examined herself to see if there was blood

phrases.english: What is 'she checked'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last words of step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'checked' means during רבי יהודה's twilight only, or during both twilights

steps.title: It cannot mean she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight
steps.stepSummary: If 'checked' meant only during רבי יהודה's twilight, then רבי יהודה בן אגרא would say 'no worry' even when she checked during neither. But then she did not check at all, so that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight and not during רבי יוסי's, that would mean רבי יהודה בן אגרא holds that even if she checked during neither one, she does not worry. But she did not check at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning and throws it out, the same way it did in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי accepts רבי יוסי's strict version only when she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight. Then רבי יהודה בן אגרא, who is lenient in this ברייתא, would be lenient in the case with less checking, meaning no check at all. Being lenient when she never checked makes no sense, so this reading fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say': introduces a suggestion that will be tested
'From this it follows': drawing an implication
During רבי יהודה's twilight, the earlier בין השמשות

phrases.english: If you say that she checked during Rabbi Yehuda's,
and did not check during Rabbi Yosei's,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא סָבַר
phrases.english: it follows that Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra holds
that even though she did not check

phrases.aramaic: לָא בִּדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא בִּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: neither during Rabbi Yehuda's nor during Rabbi Yosei's —
she does not worry?
But she did not check!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'checked' means only during רבי יהודה's twilight
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make רבי יהודה בן אגרא lenient even when she never checked at all

steps.title: So 'checked' means during both twilights
steps.stepSummary: So 'checked' must mean she checked during both twilights. It follows that רבי יהודה בן אגרא holds that if she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's, she does not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that she checked during both רבי יהודה's twilight and רבי יוסי's. From this it follows that רבי יהודה בן אגרא holds: if she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's, she does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the second meaning: she checked during both twilights. It then draws out what רבי יהודה בן אגרא must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees with רבי יוסי's strict version only when she checked during both twilights. So רבי יהודה בן אגרא, who disagrees, must be the lenient one in the in-between case, where she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not רבי יוסי's. Yet in the first ברייתא (step 15), רבי יהודה בן אגרא is the one who worries in exactly that in-between case. The next step spells out this clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, it is obvious': after the first option fails, the other one must be right
She does not worry

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names: רבי יהודה בן אגרא is the sage who disagrees with רבי, while 'רבי יהודה's twilight' refers to a different sage's definition of בין השמשות.
steps.whatToRemember: In the stain ברייתא, 'checked' means she checked during both twilights. So here רבי יהודה בן אגרא is lenient when she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight. In the first ברייתא he worries in that same case.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
that she checked both during Rabbi Yehuda's
and during Rabbi Yosei's,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא סָבַר:
phrases.english: it follows that Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra holds:
if she checked during Rabbi Yehuda's
and did not check during Rabbi Yosei's —
she does not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא דְּבָדְקָה בֵּין בִּדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וּבֵין בִּדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 rejects the first meaning, this gives the remaining meaning and its result
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Checked' means during both twilights, so רבי יהודה בן אגרא is lenient when she checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading makes רבי יהודה בן אגרא lenient in a case where the first ברייתא had him worry, so the contradiction raised in step 16 is now in place.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's twilight is night for רבי יהודה בן אגרא, a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: From the previous step, the גמרא concludes that for רבי יהודה בן אגרא, רבי יוסי's twilight counts as night. That contradicts another statement of רבי יהודה בן אגרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that, for רבי יהודה בן אגרא, the twilight of רבי יוסי counts as night. But then one statement of רבי יהודה בן אגרא contradicts another statement of his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes what it just proved and draws a conclusion: for רבי יהודה בן אגרא, רבי יוסי's twilight counts as real night. It then points out that this clashes with something else he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is lenient even when she did not check during רבי יוסי's later twilight. So that moment must count as night for him, and seeing then would not add a day. But in the first ברייתא, he worries in exactly that case, which treats רבי יוסי's twilight as a doubt. So the same תנא seems to hold two opposite positions.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently; so we see. Used to draw a conclusion from what was just said.
Twilight, the in-between time after sunset that may be day or night.
Night
A difficulty; a contradiction that needs an answer.

phrases.english: Evidently, the twilight of Rabbi Yosei

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא — לֵילְיָא הוּא.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra, is night.
There is a contradiction: Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra's statement
against Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra's other statement!
phrases.notes: He means the earlier ברייתא in his name, which did not treat twilight as definitely night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא — לֵילְיָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 20's reading of 'she checked' and turns it into a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה בן אגרא's two statements.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי's twilight is night for him in one ברייתא, it cannot be uncertain or not-night for him in the other.

steps.title: Without רבי's addition this could be answered, but with it the difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: Without רבי's addition, the two ברייתות could be explained as two different cases. But רבי's addition blocks that answer, so the contradiction remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, without רבי's statement there would be no difficulty. There, she checked during רבי יהודה's twilight but not during רבי יוסי's. Here, she checked during both רבי יהודה's and רבי יוסי's. But according to רבי's statement, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא considers an easy way out of the contradiction, splitting the two ברייתות into two different cases. It then explains why רבי's statement makes that easy answer fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy answer says the first ברייתא, where רבי יהודה בן אגרא worries, covers a woman who checked only during רבי יהודה's twilight. The stain ברייתא, where he is lenient, would cover a woman who checked during both. But רבי says the strict view is right only where she checked during both. That means רבי יהודה בן אגרא's disagreement, and his leniency, must be in the partial-check case. So the two cases cannot be split, and the contradiction stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this part works fine. It sets up a contrast with a part that does not work.
She checked herself.
There / here. Used to point to two different sources or cases.

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who said he heard from רבי יוסי. He is not רבי יהודה, whose twilight is being discussed.

phrases.english: Granted, without the statement of Rabbi,
phrases.notes: This is רבי's addition from step 17: 'this view is correct where she checked.'

phrases.english: it is not difficult:
there, it is where she checked during Rabbi Yehuda's twilight
and did not check during Rabbi Yosei's twilight;
here, it is where she checked as well
during Rabbi Yehuda's twilight and during Rabbi Yosei's twilight.
But according to Rabbi's statement, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the contradiction of step 21 by ruling out a possible answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the two ברייתות speak about different cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's 'where she checked' forces the reading that רבי יהודה בן אגרא is lenient in the partial-check case, so the second ברייתא cannot be limited to a woman who checked during both twilights.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי יהודה בן אגרא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two תנאים report רבי יהודה בן אגרא's view differently. The first holds that רבי יהודה's twilight ends, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about the view of רבי יהודה בן אגרא. This תנא holds that רבי יהודה's twilight ends...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer to the contradiction: the two ברייתות come from two different תנאים who understood רבי יהודה בן אגרא differently. It starts explaining the first תנא's view, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of making both statements fit together, the גמרא says each ברייתא reflects a different report of what רבי יהודה בן אגרא held. So there is no real self-contradiction. The first תנא's view begins with the idea that רבי יהודה's twilight comes to an end, and we will see what follows from that.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים. The answer that two sages disagree, so each source follows a different one.
According to; in the opinion of.
Ends; is complete.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא settles a contradiction: the two sources are not one opinion but two reports of a sage's view.

phrases.english: There are two tanna'im
and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Yehuda ben Agra:
this tanna holds
that Rabbi Yehuda's twilight ends,

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן אַגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 21 and 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two תנאים disagree about the sage's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות give the same view of רבי יהודה בן אגרא, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא's report of רבי יהודה בן אגרא, so there is no contradiction.
